title: GDN backward, five stages
formula: d(q, k, v, beta, g) of the chunked gated delta rule with per-token log gate g, intra-chunk keep exp(g_cumsum_i - g_cumsum_j) under the causal mask, L=64 chunk, D=128, BF16 [B,H,C,64,128] inputs with FP32 accumulation and FP32 gradients
study_for: What a per-token gate costs a backward that already exists. Against delta_rule_bwd this adds one input (`g_cumsum`), one materialised [64,64] `decay_mask`, one output (`d_g`), and a gradient path that does not look like the others: `finalize_grads` in reference.py assembles d_g_cumsum from d_g_core + d_g_wu, folds the decay-mask gradient in as `(d_decay_mask * decay_mask).sum(-1) - (d_decay_mask * decay_mask).sum(-2)` — the row/column asymmetry is the i-j in the exponent — and only then runs `reverse_cumsum` to turn d_g_cumsum back into d_g.

finalize's gate reduction is batched four BHC rows at a time, so its d_g operands (`d_g_core`, `d_g_wu`, both masked decay gradients) and its d_g destination are flattened to [BHC, ...] while every other tensor stays [B,H,C,...], and four constant GM operands — `selector_rows`, `neg_selector_rows`, `eye`, `reverse_tril` — carry that batching and the reverse-causal keep. The `partition_tail` case is BHC=6 precisely because 6 is not a multiple of 4: it is the only case that runs the partial batch-tile path.

inverse_preprocess reuses the retired L0C tmp ring for d_attn after its FIX copy, and its vector stage captures each complete input row in registers before writing the results back in place — d_attn becomes d_score, decay_mask becomes d_decay, preprocess_score becomes the masked d_decay. The Cube-to-Vector credit is only returned on MTE3 after those final reads. That is 32 KiB of L0C and 40 KiB of UB bought with a read-before-write ordering, and it is the part that breaks first if you reorder the vector stage.

Two vf helpers here started life with the same name in two stage modules and are not the same function: `cast_l_rows_float_to_bf16_nz_vf` (scan_local) and `cast_l_rows_float_to_bf16_nz_barrier_vf` (inverse_preprocess) differ by a single trailing `vf_barrier(VfPipe.STORE, VfPipe.LOAD)`. Separate modules hid that; one file makes it visible.
do_not_copy_when: You do not need the gate. delta_rule_bwd is this unit evaluated at g == 0: no g_cumsum operand, no materialised decay_mask, no d_g output, and a constant strict-lower keep instead of exp(g_cumsum_i - g_cumsum_j). It is the shorter read and the better starting point.

Your chunk length is not 64 or your head dimension is not 128. L=64 / D=128 is fixed and there is no L or D tail path: the NZ fractal staging, the 16-row BF16 C0 and every on-chip budget in the five stages were sized around that pair. Only the BHC count is allowed a tail.

You need a nonzero initial state or a gradient with respect to it. This backward supports the zero-initial-state path only and d_initial_state is not in its ABI, so the boundary term you would need has no producer here.

You want the forward's preprocessing convention. This backward preserves the source's ordering, rounding `key * beta` into the BF16 cube operand before `key @ key.T`; forward-v2 applies FP32 beta after that matmul. The two saved-state generators are not bitwise interchangeable and the reference here models the backward's, not the forward's.
